Cc: Dylan Brooks <dylan_brooks@redwood.com>, Laura Bennett <laura_bennett@redwood.com>
Date: 2026-12-02T15:12:00Z
Subject: Competitive bake-off recap: Redwood vs. Competitors (Omniva Health)

Hi Kai —

Thanks again for the time today. Quick recap from our discovery so we’re aligned on pain, scope, and next steps. Please flag anything I got wrong.

Key pain points you shared:
- Current latency spikes on peak billing runs (~50–200ms p50 -> p95 jumps) causing downstream timeouts.
- High per-token inference costs for document ingestion + reranking workflows; want to reduce unit cost without losing accuracy.
- Data residency and audit requirements for PHI-adjacent metadata (SOC2 + region controls).

Goals for a winning vendor
- Meet p95 latency target of <=300ms for real-time routes and <150ms for cached paths.
- Match current quality on rerank/QA flows (we’ll use your eval set).
- Clear quantization/throughput plan that reduces cost by 30%+ vs current baseline.
- Enterprise controls: KMS integration and audit log retention >= 12 months.

Competitive snapshot (from today’s call) — items we’ll validate in bake-off:
- Redwood: strong runtime batching + prefix KV cache, quantization profiles for Ampere/Tesla, unified API for hosted/private.
- Vendor A (reference): lower latency in small batch tests but no production-grade audit logs.
- Vendor B (reference): cheaper at high throughput but worse rerank quality on your eval set.

Open questions / assumptions to validate during PoC
1) We’ll run your 3 rerank workloads + 2 long-context generation tests (docs ingestion). Can you confirm the eval files + sample size?
2) Are there any format constraints for identifiers (PII hashing) we need to apply before sending data?
3) Success criteria: p95 latency <=300ms AND rerank NDCG within 2% of baseline.

Proposed next steps
- I attached a competitive matrix and a mutual action plan template (see attachments).
- Redwood PoC: 2-week focused bake-off (week 1: config + smoke; week 2: load/quality).
- Technical kickoff: Thu 12/09 or Mon 12/13 — 60m (Redwood SE + Omniva SRE + Product).
- Redwood deliverables: test harness, runbook for quantization profiles, and a cost/latency projection.

Attachments:
- redwood-omniva-competitive-matrix.xlsx (comparison matrix)
- redwood-omniva-maf-2026.pdf (mutual action plan / SOW stub)

Thanks — I’ll wait for confirmation on the eval files and the kickoff date that works best.

Best,
Marissa Cole

Subject: Re: Competitive bake-off recap: Redwood vs. Competitors (Omniva Health)

Thanks Marissa — appreciate the clear recap. A few clarifications from our side:

- Eval files: Priya will upload the rerank eval set + two docgen samples to the shared Drive by EOD tomorrow. Priya: can you confirm when the sample ids and README are live?
- PII: we can provide hashed identifiers. We don’t need raw PHI in the test harness; will provide hashed IDs and a mapping file stored in our secure bucket if needed.
- Success criteria: agreed on the p95 and NDCG thresholds. For cost projections, we want a modeled run at our average daily throughput (approx 4M tokens/day) in addition to peak tests.

We’re assigning a POA (proof-of-action) to this: if Redwood can show equivalent or better NDCG on our rerank set with projected cost improvement >=30% and meet the latency targets in the week-2 load test, we move to a pilot contract.

Kickoff: 12/09 works well for the team — 10:00am PT.

Looking forward — Kai
